356298.title: Nongsiang–Saikia order conjecture for non-nilpotent graphs
356298.literal_statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite non-nilpotent groups. For a group $K$, let $\mathfrak{R}_K$ denote the graph obtained from the graph on $K$ in which $x$ and $y$ are adjacent exactly when $\langle x,y\rangle$ is not nilpotent by removing isolated vertices. **Nongsiang–Saikia conjecture.** If

$$
\mathfrak{R}_G \simeq \mathfrak{R}_H,
$$

then

$$
|G|=|H|.
$$

This is a weaker version of the false conjecture that isomorphic non-nilpotent graphs determine the groups themselves up to isomorphism. The supplied text does not state whether the Nongsiang–Saikia conjecture has been resolved.

356345.title: Myers's conjecture on a three-color Rado number
356345.literal_statement:
Let $R_3(\mathcal{E})$ denote the smallest $n$ such that every 3-coloring of $[n]$ induces a monochromatic solution to the equation $\mathcal{E}$. For $m\ge 3$, consider the equation $x-y=(m-2)z$. **Myers's conjecture.**

$$
R_3(x-y=(m-2)z)=m^3-m^2-m-1.
$$

This conjecture gives exact values for a family of generalized Schur-related Rado numbers. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.

356361.title: The maximum VC-dimension conjecture for bounded-index power subgroups
356361.literal_statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer of bounded index, meaning $r\ll 1$, and let

$$
\Gamma^{(r)}=\{x^r:x\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^\times
$$

be the subgroup of $r$th powers in the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Define

$$
\alpha_q^{(r)}=\frac{\operatorname{VCdim}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\Gamma^{(r)})}{\log_2q},\qquad \underline{\alpha}^{(r)}=\liminf_{q\to\infty}\alpha_q^{(r)}.
$$

**Maximum VC-dimension conjecture for power subgroups.** One has

$$
\underline{\alpha}^{(r)}=1.
$$

Consequently, $\operatorname{VCdim}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\Gamma^{(r)})=(1+o_r(1))\log_2q$ as $q\to\infty$. This is stated as the bounded-index generalization of the quadratic-residue expectation; the supplied text says that analogous partial progress is proved, but does not give a resolution of the conjecture.

terms: The maximum VC-dimension conjecture for bounded-index power subgroups

356361.assessment_and_remaining_lemmas: Bounded index power subgroup/translation VC asymptotics needs r restrictions and limiting field family. r=1 endpoint is a scope correction, not credited. Primary definitions unread.

356391.title: The slice-rank conjecture for group multiplication tensors
356391.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M(G)$ denote its matching number, and define the minimum slice rank

$$
\operatorname{SR}(G)=\min_k \operatorname{SR}(T_{k[G]}),
$$

where the minimum is over algebraically closed fields $k$ and $T_{k[G]}$ is the multiplication tensor of the group algebra $k[G]$. **The slice-rank conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{SR}(G)\leq M(G)\cdot |G|^{o(1)}.
$$

This would make the minimum slice rank of the group multiplication tensor essentially controlled by the largest matching in the group and would yield corresponding slice-rank bounds for matching problems in groups. The source describes this as a conjecture slightly weaker than one previously proposed by Petrov; no resolution is supplied here.

356399.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian cycle conjecture for strongly edge-colored graphs
356399.literal_statement: Let $G^c$ be a strongly edge-colored graph with $n$ vertices, where strongly edge-colored means that any two adjacent edges and any two edges joined by an edge have distinct colors. Its degree is the usual graph degree. **Rainbow Hamiltonian cycle conjecture.** Every strongly edge-colored graph $G^c$ with $n$ vertices and degree at least $\frac{n+1}{2}$ has a rainbow Hamiltonian cycle. This conjecture proposes a Dirac-type minimum-degree condition guaranteeing a rainbow Hamiltonian cycle in a strongly edge-colored graph; the source presents it as an open conjecture.

356404.title: Brualdi–Quinn bipartite strong edge-coloring conjecture
356404.literal_statement:

$$
\chi^s(G)\le\Delta_A\Delta_B.
$$

356410.title: Conjecture on largest minimum distances of binary self-orthogonal codes of dimension 5
356410.literal_statement:
Let $d(n,k)$ denote the largest minimum distance of a binary linear $[n,k]$ code, and let $d_{so}(n,k)$ denote the largest minimum distance of a binary self-orthogonal $[n,k]$ code. If

$$
n=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left\lceil \frac{d}{2^i} \right\rceil
$$

for $d$ a single even integer, then **the largest-minimum-distance conjecture.**

$$
d_{so}(n,k)=d(n,k)-2.
$$

Otherwise,

$$
d_{so}(n,k)=2\left\lfloor \frac{d(n,k)}{2} \right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture predicts the largest minimum distances of binary self-orthogonal codes from the corresponding unrestricted binary linear-code distances. The supplied text gives supporting results for several dimension-$5$ parameter pairs, but provides no resolution of the general claim.

356417.title: Unbounded handle complexity conjecture for connected sums of the Poincaré sphere
356417.literal_statement: Let $Y_n=\#_n\Sigma(2,3,5)$, where $\Sigma(2,3,5)$ is the Poincaré homology sphere. This would generalize the paper's lower bounds for the numbers of $1$-, $2$-, and $3$-handles, and concerns the complexity of bounding four-manifolds even though $Y_n\#-Y_n$ bounds an integer homology ball.

356464.title: The Weak $(n,k,t)$-Conjecture on minimum $(n,k,t)$-graphs
356464.literal_statement:
Let $n,k,t$ be positive integers with $n\geq k\geq t$. A graph $G$ is an **$(n,k,t)$-graph** if $|V(G)|=n$ and every induced subgraph on $k$ vertices contains a clique on $t$ vertices; a **minimum** $(n,k,t)$-graph is one with the minimum number of edges among all such graphs. **Weak $(n,k,t)$-Conjecture.** There exists a minimum $(n,k,t)$-graph that is a disjoint union of cliques.

This is the existential version of the structural conjecture for minimum $(n,k,t)$-graphs, generalizing the complemented form of Turán's theorem. The paper proves the stronger assertion that every minimum $(n,k,t)$-graph is a disjoint union of cliques.

356634.title: Inner-corner obstruction conjecture for four-dimensional polydisks
356634.literal_statement:

356642.title: Herzog–Kaplan–Lev conjecture on products of cycle classes
356642.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $l\geq 3$, with either $l$ odd or $k$ even. For $2\leq l\leq n$, let $C_l$ be the conjugacy class of $l$-cycles in $S_n$, and let $n(k,l)$ be the largest natural number $n$ such that $C_l^k=A_n$.

**Herzog–Kaplan–Lev conjecture.** One has

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{2}{3}kl \right\rfloor\leq n(k,l)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{2}{3}kl\right\rfloor+1.
$$

The conjecture is false in general: the paper determines $n(k,l)$ for $k\geq 5$ and $3\nmid l$, obtaining values below the conjectured lower bound. It is nevertheless true in several cases, including $k=2,3,4$ and $3\mid l$.

356651.title: Chvátal's Erdős–Chvátal simplex conjecture
356651.literal_statement:
Let $k>r\geq 1$ and $n\geq \frac{r+1}{r}k$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ is **without an $r$-simplex** if it contains no $r$-simplex.

$$
\binom{n-1}{k-1}
$$

sets.

This conjecture asserts that the largest uniform families without an $r$-simplex are typically trivial, with the bound attained by the family of all $k$-sets containing a fixed element. Its general status is not specified in the source.

356733.title: The path extremal conjecture for the minimum edge derivative of Kemeny's constant

356744.title: Restricted Erdős–Heilbronn formula for abelian groups
356744.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of the order of $G$. For positive integers $m$ and $h$ with $m\leq p$, write $\rho\hat{\;} (G,m,h)$ for the minimum size of a restricted $h$-fold sumset of an $m$-element subset. **Restricted Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture.**

$$
\rho \hat{\;} (G,m,h)=\min\{p,hm-h^2+1\}.
$$

The formula is known for groups of prime order, while the corresponding statement for general abelian groups is presented as a potential next case and remains open.

356747.title: Matzke's equality criterion for signed sumsets in elementary abelian groups
356747.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $m,h,r$ be positive integers. Define $f_1=hm-h+1$. Let $\delta$ be $0$ or $1$ according as $p-1$ is divisible by $h$ or not. Let $k$ be the largest integer such that $p^k+\delta\leq f_1$, and let $c$ be the largest integer such that $(hc+1)p^k+\delta\leq f_1$. **Matzke's conjecture.** If $m>(c+1)p^k$, then

$$
\rho_{\pm}(\mathbb Z_p^r,m,h)>\rho(\mathbb Z_p^r,m,h).
$$

The preceding theorem proves equality under the opposite inequality; the necessity of that condition is conjectured and remains open.

$$

357101.title: No-infinite-path conjecture for the uniform infinite meandric system
357101.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal R$ be independent two-sided simple random walks on $\mathbb Z$ with $\mathcal L_0=\mathcal R_0=0$, and use them to construct the two infinite non-crossing arc diagrams of the uniform infinite meandric system (UIMS). Let the UIMS be the union of these arc diagrams, whose connected components are loops and possibly bi-infinite paths. **No-infinite-path conjecture.** Almost surely, the UIMS has no infinite path. 357105.title: The asymptotic upper-bound conjecture for the 2-tone chromatic number of planar graphs
357105.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, let $\tau_2(G)$ denote its 2-tone chromatic number, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. **Planar 2-tone bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that all planar $G$ satisfy

$$
\tau_2(G)\le \sqrt{3\Delta(G)}+C.
$$

This conjecture predicts the correct order of growth for the 2-tone chromatic number of planar graphs, with the additive constant independent of $G$.

357114.title: The equal odd-hole-length 3-colorability conjecture for triangle-free graphs
357114.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph. An **odd hole** is an induced cycle of odd length at least five, and $G$ is **triangle-free** if it has no cycle of length three. **Equal odd-hole-length conjecture.** If $G$ is triangle-free and all odd holes of $G$ have the same length, then $G$ is 3-colorable.

This would extend the known 3-colorability results for graph families whose odd holes are constrained by their girth and maximum permitted length. The source gives no resolution of this broader conjecture.
